mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points over one month signals labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns as investor sentiment deteriorates.
failure_condition: If the unemployment rate rises by >0.3pp in a month, but the S&P 500 still posts positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% month-over-month signals weakening demand in the housing sector, which may lead to broader economic weakness and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: Housing starts decline by >5% mom, but SPX posts positive 20d returns in >50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1.5% month-over-month signals strong supply-side activity, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns as production growth supports economic expansion.
failure_condition: If industrial production increases by >1.5% mom, but the S&P 500 posts negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When payroll employment (PAYEMS) increases by more than 100,000 jobs in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases, it signals a strong labor market, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns as economic growth accelerates.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >100k and UNRATE decreases
failure_condition: If payroll employment increases by >100k and UNRATE decreases, but SPX posts negative 20d returns in >40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A 0.5% quarter-over-quarter increase in real GDP (GDPC1) signals strengthening economic demand, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns as corporate earnings prospects improve.
failure_condition: If real GDP increases by >0.5% qoq, but the S&P 500 posts negative 60-day returns in more than 30% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) increases by more than 0.2pp, it signals potential monetary policy tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as interest rate expectations rise.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS is below 1% and UNRATE increases by >0.2pp, but SPX posts positive 20d returns in >40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real federal spending (RSAFS) by more than 2% month-over-month signals expanding fiscal demand, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns as government spending supports economic activity.
failure_condition: If real federal spending increases by >2% mom, but the S&P 500 posts negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases.
